name: com.qubesync/quickbooks-desktop-api
title: QuBe Sync: QuickBooks Desktop API for developers
description: Build QuickBooks Desktop integrations: validated API requests and workflows, answers by webhook.

tools.name: get_workflow_authoring_guide
tools.description: Returns the QuBeSync workflow authoring guide: the rules for writing a workflow chart (a JSON statechart that runs qbXML requests against QuickBooks Desktop), the chart JSON Schema, and a canonical example. Load this before writing or editing a chart, then check your chart with validate_workflow_chart.

tools.name: validate_workflow_chart
tools.description: Validates a workflow chart without saving or running it -- the same structural validation and lint as POST /api/v2/workflows/validate, minus the checks that need a specific app. Returns {valid, errors, warnings, workflows_to_create}. `errors` block saving/publishing and must be fixed; `warnings` are likely mistakes worth reviewing. Each issue has a `path` into the chart document (e.g. states.create.on.success.0.target) and a `message`. A `workflow` state calling a child workflow not listed in `known_workflows` is reported as a warning, and its key is listed in `workflows_to_create`: that workflow must exist and be published in the app before this chart can be published.

chart.description: The chart document to check (the JSON object with version, key, states, ...). A JSON-encoded string of it is also accepted.

known_workflows.description: Keys of workflows that already exist in the target app and that this chart may call from `workflow` states. Calls to other keys are reported as warnings.

tools.name: list_workflow_templates
tools.description: Lists the workflow chart templates QuBeSync ships (key, name, description): complete, tested charts for the common multi-step jobs. These match names -- ranked against the connection's name index (ACME, Inc. finds Acme Inc) -- and ask your app about near matches: resolve (any list record by kind and name -- a customer, a job, a vendor, an item, an account -- or the ListID it stored), ensure (resolve, then create what is missing, asking when the name is held elsewhere in its name space), upsert (resolve, then update, or create, asking as ensure does when the name is held elsewhere), push_records (many upserts) and add_transaction (any transaction add, once every customer, item, class or account it names exists: it finds each and asks every question first, then creates what is missing by a rule per kind). The rest: resolve_transaction (a transaction by id, number or GUID); record a payment (asking when it's more than the invoice owes, or the invoice isn't there); void a transaction; read the company's profile (company, preferences, host); pull every record, or those changed and deleted since a date, paged to your app (pull_changes, stream_query). A workflow runs server-side against a connection, settles requests QuickBooks never answered, asks before overwriting a record someone else changed, and can pause for a decision from your app. Workflows run on realtime and simulated connections only (a standard one answers 422 realtime_required). Install one as-is, child workflows included, with POST /api/v2/workflow-templates/{key}/install (body {"publish": true}; add "replace": true to re-install over workflows the app already has); fetch it with get_workflow_template to read or adapt it first.

tools.name: get_workflow_template
tools.description: Returns one shipped workflow chart template by key (see list_workflow_templates), with the child workflows it calls, every question it can ask (each `prompt.id`, with its options) and every way it can end, and the API calls that install and run it. Its whole usage contract, with example webhooks and answers, is GET /api/v2/workflow-templates/{key}/usage.md (or /usage for JSON), readable before anything is installed. Unmodified, install it with POST /api/v2/workflow-templates/{key}/install (body {"publish": true}), which installs its child workflows too ("replace": true re-installs over the ones the app already has); adapted (check with validate_workflow_chart), install it with PUT /api/v2/workflows/{key} (publish: true), each child first. Then run it with POST /api/v2/connections/{connection_id}/workflow-runs with an `input` matching the chart's declared inputs, on a realtime or simulated connection: a standard one answers 422 with errors.code realtime_required and nothing stored, so the same call starts the run once the connection is upgraded. An installed workflow is a copy: when the template changes later, GET /api/v2/workflows/{key} says so in template.status (update_available), and installing it again with "replace": true takes the new version.

tools.name: report_confusion
tools.description: Send feedback to the QuBe Sync team about something in this server, its guides, or the v2 API that confused you, so we can fix it. Use it when a tool description or guide was unclear or contradicted what actually happened, an error didn't say how to fix it, you had to guess a parameter, endpoint, or behavior, or you couldn't find a way to do what your user needed. Make one call per problem, after you've got past it or given up, and put what the answer turned out to be in `answer`. Not for praise, and not for bugs in your user's own app. The QuBe Sync team stores and reads these reports: never include API keys, webhook secrets, your user's code, or QuickBooks data such as customer names and amounts -- describe the problem in terms of our tools and docs.

agent.description: Your client and model, e.g. "Claude Code / claude-opus-5-5".

answer.description: What actually worked, or what the docs should have said. The most useful part of a report.

details.description: What you were trying to do, what you expected, and what happened instead.

kind.description: unclear: a description or guide left you unsure what to do. wrong: it contradicted what actually happened. unhelpful_error: an error didn't say how to fix it. missing: you couldn't find a way to do what you needed.

outcome.description: resolved: you found the right answer. worked_around: you did something else instead. blocked: you couldn't continue.

subject.description: The tool, endpoint, or guide involved, e.g. "create_invoice", "POST /api/v2/workflow-templates/{key}/install", "get_workflow_authoring_guide".

summary.description: One line naming the problem and where it is, e.g. "create_invoice: unclear whether a line's item takes a name or a ListID".

tools.name: match_records
tools.description: Finds the record in a customer's QuickBooks company file that a name means, even written differently -- QuickBooks itself only matches a name exactly, or by 'contains' on one list. Checks the arguments and returns the v2 request to send (POST /api/v2/connections/{connection_id}/matches); it never touches a connection. Matching needs a realtime or simulated connection: a standard one answers 422 matching_requires_realtime (switching a sandbox connection to realtime is free). The first match on a connection starts building its name index and answers 409 name_index_building until it's ready, a few Web Connector sessions later; POST /api/v2/connections/{connection_id}/name-index with a webhook_url to start it ahead and be sent name_index.ready. The answer's `match` is a tier: exact (the full name, as QuickBooks compares names: use `record`), strong (exactly one record is the same once punctuation, accents, company suffixes such as Inc/LLC, spacing or word order are set aside, has the same number in its name (Subway #1234 for Subway Store 1234), has the account number sent, or shares the email, phone or postal code: likely, so confirm `record` before using it), candidates (up to 10 ranked records with a score and reasons: ask which, if any) or none. Numbers in names must agree: Subway #1235 is never offered for Subway #1234. When candidates_total is more than a person can choose from (a file of numbered locations), ask for what tells them apart -- the number, city, postal_code or account_number -- and match again with it. exact_only: true answers exact or none; min_score moves the candidate threshold for one call. Match a record once: when it's confirmed, store its list_id and refer to it by that (customer_ref: {list_id}); match again only when a stored list_id stops working.

exact_only.description: true answers only exact or none, never a fuzzy match, so the answer can be used without asking.

fields.description: For customer, vendor, employee, other_name, entity only: what else the app knows. The same account_number makes a strong match whatever the name. The same email, phone or postal_code, with a name at least 0.4 alike, makes a strong match. company_name and city only rank a candidate higher. city and postal_code are the record's billing (or main) address's. company_name isn't taken for employee.

kind.description: Which lists to look in. entity is customers, vendors, employees and other names together (one name space in QuickBooks); item is every item type.

min_score.description: This call's candidate threshold, in place of 0.44: raise it to list only close names, lower it to list more. Not with exact_only.

name.description: The name the app has for the record: its own name, without its parent's when parent is given.

parent.description: For a job, sub-item, subaccount and the like: the parent's full name or ListID, so only its children match. Taken for customer, entity, item, account, class, customer_type, vendor_type, job_type.

tools.name: get_integration_checklist
tools.description: Returns QuBe Sync's integration checklist as Markdown: the 57 rules an app integrating with QuBe Sync has to get right (verifying webhook signatures on the raw body, answering 2xx within 5 seconds and working in a job, a new run reference saved before the start, revisions and delivery ids, never answering a run's question for the user, QuickBooks ids keyed by their connection and list, lost answers, webhooks not polling...). Each has an id, a severity, when it applies, why, what to check in the code, what wrong and right look like, and its docs. Read it before writing or reviewing an integration's webhook handler, run starts or stored QuickBooks ids. Pass `area` for one area's rules. To audit a whole codebase, a coding agent can follow the audit skill at https://qubesync.com/skills/qube-sync-audit/SKILL.md, which has every rule.

area.description: One area's rules only: onboarding (Onboarding); starting-runs (Calling the API and starting runs); webhooks (Webhooks); questions (Questions and endings); data (Stored QuickBooks data); quickbooks (QuickBooks behaviour); going-live (Going live). Leave it out for every rule.

tools.name: create_account
tools.description:
This message allows you to perform the same activities as a user does in the QB New Account form, which can be accessed in QB by selecting Lists->Chart of Accounts->Accounts->New. If you want the account to be a subaccount to an existing account, similar to using the SubAccount checkbox and selection list drop down in the New Account form, you use the `parent_ref` aggregate. Notice that the `parent_ref` can take either the parent account’s `list_id` or `full_name`.

The `account_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3000 invalid_object_id, 3040 invalid_amount, 3070 string_too_long, 3100 name_in_use, 3120 object_not_found, 3140 invalid_reference, 3150 missing_element, 3175 in_use, 3176 locked, 3180 cannot_save, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3263 read_only_access, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required, 3270 missing_posting_account

tools.name: create_ar_refund_credit_card

Adds a credit card refund transaction that is linked to one or more QuickBooks credit memo transactions. You can link the credit card refund to one or more of those credit transactions.

The `ar_refund_credit_card_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

tools.name: create_credit_card_credit
tools.description:
If a QuickBooks user returns merchandise and receives credit, the credit is entered in QuickBooks and assigned to the appropriate expense account. Typically, the assigned expense account reflects the same account, customer, and class that were assigned when the merchandise was first purchased. tools.name: create_customer

tools.name: create_data_ext
tools.description:
Writes data to one data extension. This request can only be invoked if a data extension definition has already been defined for the target object type. That is, before you can perform the DataExtAdd on a particular customer, say John Henry, the data extension must already be defined for the Customer object. Notice that a data extension definition can be defined in either of two ways: via DataExtDefAdd as already described, or via the QuickBooks UI by the user specifying a custom field. Only custom fields can be defined through the UI, not private data extensions.

The `data_ext_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

tools.name: execute_list_merge
tools.description:
This request merges one list object into another list object of the same type. Currently you can merge customers/jobs, or vendors, or accounts. The consequence of the merge is that only the merge-to object remains. The merge-from object goes away and all transactions that reference that merge-from object now reference only the merge-to object.

Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3150 missing_element, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required

tools.name: execute_txn_void
tools.description:
Voids a transaction: QuickBooks keeps it, with its amounts and its lines' quantities at zero and "VOID: " in front of its memo, while deleting one removes it completely. A voided invoice keeps its number and reads back as paid. An invoice that payments paid can be voided too: each payment stays, and what it had applied to the invoice becomes its unused payment, to apply elsewhere or refund (observed on QuickBooks Enterprise 24.0, 2026-10-10).

Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

tools.name: record_payment
tools.description:
Records a customer's payment. Set `customer_ref`, `total_amount` and either `is_auto_apply` (true: to an invoice of that exact amount, else the oldest; false: to none) or `applied_to_txn_add`: each invoice's `txn_id` and amount, at most what it owes (more fails with 3210 `invalid_value`); the rest is unused_payment. A line can also apply a credit memo (`set_credit`); a `total_amount` of 0 that only does that creates no payment and answers just each invoice's txn_id and txn_type. Without `ref_number` a payment gets no number; without `deposit_to_account_ref` it goes to Undeposited Funds.

The `receive_payment_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

tools.name: update_item_discount
tools.description:
Modifies a discount item. Starting with qbXML spec 7.0, you can modify the account ref, using the `account_ref` aggregate and the `apply_account_ref_to_existing_txns` boolean. You need to use the `apply_account_ref_to_existing_txns` boolean because the QuickBooks UI displays a prompt asking whether the change should apply to existing transactions or not. Specifying True for the boolean basically dismisses this with a “Yes” answer, allowing your changes to be made and changes any existing transactions that use the item with that `account_ref`.

The `item_discount_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3000 invalid_object_id, 3040 invalid_amount, 3070 string_too_long, 3100 name_in_use, 3120 object_not_found, 3140 invalid_reference, 3150 missing_element, 3170 cannot_modify, 3175 in_use, 3176 locked, 3200 stale_edit_sequence, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3263 read_only_access, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required

tools.name: update_workers_comp_code
tools.description:
Requires the company to be subscribed to Intuit Payroll service. Modifies an existing workers’ compensation code. Notice that if a future date exists and you write a new one (using the Mod request) then the most recently written code wins.

The `workers_comp_code_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3000 invalid_object_id, 3040 invalid_amount, 3070 string_too_long, 3100 name_in_use, 3120 object_not_found, 3150 missing_element, 3170 cannot_modify, 3175 in_use, 3176 locked, 3200 stale_edit_sequence, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3263 read_only_access, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required

edit_sequence.description: `edit_sequence` is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current `edit_sequence`.

include_qbxml.description: Also return the qbXML this compiles to, for debugging. Not part of the v2 request.

is_active.description: If `is_active` is true, this object is currently enabled for use by QuickBooks. The default value is true.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.

name.description: Name is the case-insensitive short name of a list object (without ancestors). It must be unique within its hierarchy scope.

effective_date.description: Specifies the date at which the workers’ comp code and it’s related premium goes into effect.
